questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Amsterdam as my study destination because it sounded like an interesting city to live in, it was pretty close to home and the country/city has a high proficiency in english

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I feel like it as pretty easy. The university of Amsterdam had a pretty helpful website for exchange and i recieved alot of emails with relevant information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: During the introduction day i met the international office of my faculty.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy since i got housing through the university raffle. So personally i had very little dificulties but i have heard that the Amsterdam housing market is very tough.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You will most likely have to spend at least an hour each day on comuting.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The registration proces was a bit messy, since the first course application was not binding, so i applied for too many courses in the first block. When i got to the actual application proces i all of sudden could not apply for the same courses so i had to rush to find new ones.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: In the first round of registration of I filled out a written form the courses i wanted to do. Later on i was invited to a google forms, where I could chose courses for first and second block from a list.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I contacted the university of Amsterdam about how I was not able to register for the courses I had planned on doing. They said that it was not realistic to do 4 courses in one block. So instead the advised me to have 3 courses in each block.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I did not get all the courses I initially thought but it worked out in the end

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can only get 3 courses in each block.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was quite alright, not too hard neither too easy. Some of the master courses in the second semester are somewhat build on thing learned in the first semester of the master. But it is possible to catch up.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching focused more on active participation and oral presentations. It was fun but you had to get used to initially.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. Economic growth
2. Human development
3. Neuroeconomics
4. Industrial Organisation
5. Sustainable Finance
6. International business

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Neuroeconomics is very interesting but also very difficult since it basically like doing a neuroscience course with a bit of economics mixed in. You also have to do a interesting but difficult oral presentation.
Human development is also very interesting and the oral presentation based on a scientific article was challenging but fun.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Renting a bike each month only costs 20 euros which was less than I expected. I personally did not pay that much for housing but I have heard some crazy stories.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The cafes at uni are good. There was good athletic activities but I did not participate in any.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I dont think I can think of any

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would try to visit as many dutch cities as possible, they are all very pretty and nice.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy especially since the amount of foreign students is very high.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Try to find foreigners who are studying there for their entire master. They are often more talkative than the Dutch.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Dutch people stick to themselves, so you will be disappointed if you go here thinking you will get a ton of Dutch friends.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The campus is very international so you dont feel like you stick out just because you are an exchange student.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. You can only have three courses in each block.
2. The exams are difficult so make sure you prepare well for them.
3. Be prepared to do oral presentations. They are mandatory in alot of courses.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
1. You can only have three courses in each block.
2. The exams are difficult so make sure you prepare well for them.
3. Be prepared to do oral presentations. They are mandatory in alot of courses.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to learn people from a lot of different countires.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The exams are difficult and you have to be prepared to do long presentations in English.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
